_comment: THE REGISTRY OF VOCABULARIES. This is L-14 applied to the framework's own vocabularies:
every shared token set in this corpus is listed here once, with its declared home.
It exists because the same defect happened twice. AMENDS D-015 records the confidence
vocabulary shipping with three different memberships within hours of writing the law
against exactly that. D-019 added a fourth record class and ten sites went on saying
three for four days. The amendment's own closing line was 'Not built. next: build it if
the drift recurs.' It recurred. This is the gate.
Adding a vocabulary to the corpus without adding it here is the failure this file cannot
catch. That is a known limit, stated rather than hidden.
RULE FOR AUTHORS, learned 2026-07-26 (D-036, O-21, O-22): any vocabulary declaring
count_nouns needs exempt_files for DECISIONS.md and OBSERVATIONS.md from the start. Both are
append-only. Both quote counts verbatim as their whole purpose - a ledger entry records what
was true when written, and an observation log that cannot quote the defect it saw is not a
log. Neither has a legal edit that clears a counted-prose failure, so without the exemption
the gate cannot go green, and a gate that cannot go green teaches you to ignore it.
This happened TWICE in one sitting: adding L-18 tripped DECISIONS.md, and registering
conditional_artifact tripped OBSERVATIONS.md via the very observation recording the first
trip. Two instances is a pattern, not yet a mechanism (L-17 escalates on the THIRD). If it
recurs, the response is a check that FAILS when a count_nouns vocabulary lacks those two
exemptions - not a third hand-written exemption.

vocabularies.name: confidence
vocabularies.note: Framework-level. ACCEPTED is the member that goes missing every time; see AMENDS D-015 for why.

allowed_subsets.reason: The four verdicts a verifier may emit. UNVERIFIED is the state a claim arrives in; ACCEPTED is the operator's call. Documented in the file itself.

exempt_files.reason: Append-only. D-015's original five-token entry is the incident record itself and is never edited; the AMENDS entry above it carries the correction.
Append-only. Entries quote the defective text they observed, verbatim, which is the point of an observation log.

vocabularies.name: record_class
vocabularies.note: append-only is its own class, not a flavour of frozen (D-019). This is the vocabulary whose recurrence built this gate.

exempt_files.reason: Frozen record dated 2026-07-20, predates D-019. Annotated by addendum, never edited (L-13).
Append-only. Historical entries record what was believed when written and are never edited.
Append-only. O-1 quotes the three-class text verbatim because that is the defect it observed. An observation log that cannot quote what it saw is not a log.

vocabularies.name: law
vocabularies.note: Not a token vocabulary but the same failure applies: adding or retiring a law leaves every counted 'laws' sentence in the corpus wrong, and nothing announces it. L-18 arrived 2026-07-26 (D-034) and cost exactly two prose edits plus this line, which is the whole argument for the counted-prose check.
vocabularies.unchecked_reason: Law IDs appear as citations on nearly every page. Enumeration matching would be all false positives. Home-membership and the counted-prose check both apply.

exempt_files.reason: Append-only. D-029 quotes `the seventeen laws` as an EXAMPLE of the counted-prose form the gate learned to read; the count was true when written. Editing it to say eighteen would falsify the incident record (L-13). Added 2026-07-26 when the first law since seeding made the conflict real — see D-036.
Append-only, for the same reason and by the same pattern as record_class. An observation log that cannot quote the count it saw is not a log.

vocabularies.name: severity
vocabularies.note: Per-item scale. Orthogonal to blast radius (D-018) — never mix them in one field.

vocabularies.name: loop_phase
vocabularies.note: ACT is the phase with no skill. If an enumeration drops one, it is usually this one.

exempt_files.reason: Frozen record. Notes that the source projects ran four-phase loops without a distinct RECORD step — that is the historical fact D-013 diverged from, not drift.

vocabularies.name: id_prefix
vocabularies.note: Record IDs are permanent addresses and are never reused — distinct from filename slots, which may be refilled. S- (source document) and E- (outbound request) arrived with the source manifest and query log.
vocabularies.unchecked_reason: Bare prefixes appear constantly in prose as part of live IDs (D-19, O-4). Enumeration matching would be almost entirely false positives. Home-membership is still checked.

vocabularies.name: non_delegable
vocabularies.note: Four inherited from VOC plus Preference, which is an Astronomer addition and is single-authored.
vocabularies.unchecked_reason: Members are multi-word phrases rendered differently per site (table rows, prose lists, skill bullets). No reliable tight-run pattern. Home-membership is checked; cross-site consistency is a manual review item.

vocabularies.name: evidence_tier
vocabularies.note: Project-level, not framework-level (D-021). Projects are expected to replace this set; the check enforces internal consistency of the default only.

vocabularies.name: effort
vocabularies.unchecked_reason: Single-letter members cannot be distinguished from ordinary prose by any pattern. Wholly unchecked, deliberately. If effort drifts, only review will catch it.

vocabularies.name: verification_grade
vocabularies.unchecked_reason: The grades are rendered two ways in the corpus — as bold single words (Direct/Proxy/Derived) and as full phrases (proven in the real environment / checked in a proxy / reasoned from the source). Until one form is canonical this cannot be checked without false positives. Known gap; see tools/README.md.

vocabularies.name: attestation_grade
vocabularies.note: How much evidence stands behind a rule -- ORTHOGONAL to whether it binds (D-039). Every law binds at every tier regardless of grade. The middle member is the one D-039 added: the charter defined one and three and twelve of eighteen laws sat at two. Per-law values live in provenance/attestation.json and are checked by check_attestation() in tools/check-corpus.py.
vocabularies.unchecked_reason: Members are ordinary English words -- 'practice' and 'settled' appear constantly in prose across the corpus in unrelated senses. Any tight-run pattern would be almost entirely false positives. Home-membership, counted prose, and the per-law registry check all apply, and the registry check is the strong one.

exempt_files.reason: Append-only, per the authors' rule above: every count_nouns vocabulary needs this. Entries record what was believed when written and are never edited.
Append-only, same rule. An observation log that cannot quote the count it saw is not a log.

vocabularies.name: conditional_artifact
vocabularies.note: Gated on circumstance, not stakes — required from Lite upward once the condition holds. Registered 2026-07-26 (D-037) because adding the fifth left 'Four conditional artifacts' wrong in the home file and nothing announced it. That sentence was the ONLY thing that had to change and the gate could not see it, which is precisely the failure this registry exists to close.
vocabularies.unchecked_reason: Members are multi-word phrases rendered as table rows and as prose. No reliable tight-run pattern, same as non_delegable. Home-membership and counted prose both apply.

exempt_files.reason: Append-only. O-22 quotes `up to four conditional artifacts` because that is the drift site it observed. An observation log that cannot quote what it saw is not a log.
Append-only, pre-emptively and by the same pattern as every other counted vocabulary. Entries record what was believed when written and are never edited.

vocabularies.name: capability_rule
vocabularies.note: Prefixed K- (capability) rather than I- on purpose: the first consuming project numbers six invariants I-1..I-6, and a bare I-3 would resolve to two things (L-2). Same counted-prose hazard as the law set.
vocabularies.unchecked_reason: Rule IDs appear as citations in prose. Enumeration matching would be mostly false positives. Home-membership and the counted-prose check both apply.

vocabularies.name: capability_role
vocabularies.note: The DEFAULT set. Projects add and strike roles (D-035); the check enforces internal consistency of the default only, exactly as evidence_tier does. count_nouns is deliberately 'capability roles' and not 'roles' — the latter would collide with the Operator/Coordinator/Executor/Verifier set.
vocabularies.unchecked_reason: Members are multi-word phrases rendered as table rows in the home and as prose elsewhere. No reliable tight-run pattern, same as non_delegable.
